title: Would you be ok with making 0$?
author: klas-klattermus
selftext:
Tl;Dr: would you be ok with making 0$ or little money from the games you make? And do you already have a job that lets you live comfortably?

I'm messing around a bit with game dev AI and have completed a couple of simple games, and it was pretty fun! I never tried monetizing, mostly because I fall into the category of people who likes "crazy" ideas and already have an income that lets me and my family live at a lower-middle class standard.

Given the amount of awesome prototypes that I've seen and also amount of games I see being released, obviously we will have more people expressing themselves through games and also more competition for commercial products. What I wonder however, is how many of you guys do it for the love of the game and who here is looking for financial freedom or maybe fame and attention?

Can we have a little discussion about your expectations of AI game dev?

comments.author: phira
comments.body: I don't expect to make any money off it. Let's face it, I'm spending money not making it. It's fun tho, I'm having a blast and learning and making things I love to play

replies.author: jildos_legoplanet
replies.body: Exactly this. I’m learning every day while having fun. That’s what a hobby is, and hobbies usually cost some $

replies.author: Felfedezni
replies.body: Average hobby in America runs around 100-200 a month. So a 20x plan fits within that category.

replies.author: pspahn
replies.body: I expect to make nothing. I use this hobby to learn new dev paradigms, and right now there's clearly _that_ going on, and it helps me stay relevant.

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body: Same here, it's an expensive hobby but not as expensive as Warhammer or MTG :D

comments.author: account009988
comments.body: No

comments.author: DoctorBrandonLau
comments.body: Depends on how much effort I put in/and how good the results are

comments.author: LudwigLoewenlunte
comments.body:
yes have a job. just doing it for fun and because i want to play what i make and it does not exist yet. also exploring cross marketing, mobile etc. it is just pure (expensive) fun. 

for everything i have i invested 230$ and currently made 0 - but nothing is out yet

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body:
My goal is to have some people genuinely enjoy what I build.  Dream goal is to change their lives.  Money?  Only exists to allow me to keep seeking that dream.  

When AI makes money obsolete, I'll be making games.

comments.author: anon999387
comments.body: The choice will be made for you shortly because the barrier to entry to gamedev will soon be so negligible that the "value" of games will crater. There will be great pushback on the concept of a $70 game once they are made in an automated fashion with little human effort or time expended.

replies.author: Torschlusspaniker
replies.body:
Agreed. 

It is like the The Interstellar Paradox. 

Everyone today is building with the slowest and worst tools there will ever be. In a years time all the work and time you put into your tool will be just be a few prompts eclipsing what you did within minutes. 

I was smacked in the head with that fact again today. I have been working on a wifi tool for months that is like unifi designer crossed with pascal editor and I have seen 3 projects already that beat me on graphics and unifi just replicated all but 3 of my networking features within weeks of their last release. (Take a look at [https://dgreenheck.github.io/tidewater/](https://dgreenheck.github.io/tidewater/) , he did it in no time at all)

I made a lot of choices on how the app works but from when I started to now but today's AI could have made many of those choices and leap frog all the work I did in the past.

It hit me that there is no long term monetary value in any tool now.

replies.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
replies.body:
It makes me very excited, but seeing everything I loved to do become so instantly automated... I'm not quite sure how to feel. I love the speed in which I can create things, but I can't help but feel like that line from the Incredibles:

"And when everyone's super....  
no one will be...."

comments.author: Relevant-Positive-48
comments.body:
Before AI coding was a thing, I released 4 indie games in addition to trying and failing to build more than a dozen others over multiple decades.  I made a total of $130 USD on them.

I'm inspired by every success story out there and you might be one but I promise you my story is far more common than the Undertales and Stardew Valleys out there.

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body: Oh yes, being a developer and being a businessperson are definitely a small spot on the Venn diagram

comments.author: takshit2
comments.body: This is like a new expensive hobby now. Rather than buying games, I spend money building games I love playing lol

replies.author: artuuR2
replies.body: You get all excited to have it finished to play it for about 60% of the development, and then you find it's not interesting anymore and start a new one lol.

replies.author: takshit2
replies.body: That is true. Lol we enjoy building more than actually playing it 🤣

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body:
Which is totally ok!
I remember some 20?-ish years ago when I got Minecraft. I got bored after a day but I kept building mods for it for a long time and had a blast

comments.author: Plane_Friend24
comments.body:
yes. 

I even believe artists are mostly overpaid. People message me trying to get commision for one piece of work that will cost the same as an asset bundle pack i can get anywhere else that will include someone elses 20 years of experience bundled into 1.  the people who have been in it for this many years can afford competitive pricing that the newbies will never beat and now with ai, people are getting better at making their own art...   so now even the vets are having issues. 

I also experienced this when smart phones first came out. I was one of the first devs in the playstore and it was great for a time. now there is 100 apps of every possible idea.   your competiting in an endless ocean of oversaturated app of every niche.   Same thing with web dev. The united states may only have 350 million people but the entire world has many many billions more.   In the online world anyone can charge for anything and at any price. you just cant beat the competitive pricing market.   And now even the competition by numbers are going to be exagerated even more in web design because of how easy it is for anyone to make their own website for a few dollars without having to pay a professional web dev who was promised thousands per website when they attenteded their 2008 web course bootcamp.  

  
being comfortable with making $0 is all about accepting the reality of things, accept the competition, accept the market.  The market is always evolving, every few years something new comes out that people can capitlize on if they want but over time, the competition just gets too much.  Take the game runescape for example. Its easier to grind out your highest gp per hour method and buy an expensive skill than it is to train that skill using cheap methods.   you can achieve the same goal in 100 hours or 1,000 hours.    so if we applied that to life, wouldnt it just be easier to secure a steady paycheck/job. then do ai game dev as a hobby, if it makes you money great, but if it doesnt, at least your bills are paid and you dont have to get depression over it. especially when you zoom out and look around and outside your own bias and bubble , it all feels a bit silly to get upset over.

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body: Yeah, it would be great if we could make a more fair world so people wouldn't feel a need to make apps and games to make money

comments.author: JohnSnowHenry
comments.body:
Yes and yes.

I make games as an hobbie. Not expecting to get money, for that there are hundreds of better jobs to focus your time on

comments.author: EpicOfBrave
comments.body:
Yes, this lesson is very important.

Don’t live in a delusion you will become millionaire by making a software app.

comments.author: JCBAwesomist
comments.body: Would love to be able to quit my job and work full time on making games but I'm not optimistic.

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: I make things with AI for my own enjoyment. If some money comes in due to that enjoyment that is just gravy.

comments.author: Ball_Analytics
comments.body: I wouldn’t mind a $ but it’s a passion project, Im no longer comfortable by any means though at least I have time for this.

comments.author: ByteBandit_45
comments.body:
My plan is to make my wave shooter (like cod zombies but not with zombies enemies) free to play. Its way more worth for me if my game is played instead earning $10 with it. 

So my reward is build a community instead making money. Can be done with second release if my plan works out.

comments.author: MotivatedforGames
comments.body: My goal is to receive feedback and recoup all costs. Turning a profit would be amazing but my main ordeal is ensuring I get big enough consensus as well as financial recoupments.

comments.author: RickRelentless
comments.body: Independent game dev is something masochistic people do because they just can’t help themselves. If you only make games to make money you are so much better off doing pretty much anything else. You’d make more per hour working at a bar or literally doing door dash or uber then 95% of video games make.

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body: Amen, same goes for most app development I bet

comments.author: Itchy-Individual3536
comments.body: Absolutely. I've enjoyed a lot of free and open source games, and as long as I have no cost (or at least no running costs, or not more than I can write off as investing in a hobby or investing in learning) I'm happy when others enjoy what I made.

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body: I only make games for me. Much much less stressful, and I can do what I want when I want as much as I want.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: My friend donated to my [game](https://vibecodedgames.itch.io/pavement). And I'm still spending more on A.I. than I'm making.

comments.author: Calm-Shirt214
comments.body: Yes, its ok for me. I love building articial lego.

comments.author: siberianmi
comments.body:
My expectations are zero dollars, I’m here for the fun of creating things and seeing how far I can push the models.

My day to day job pays me more than enough this just fun for me and an interesting way to spend some time.

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
Living comfortably and so is my cat so I don't need to be some breakout viral success to put food on table or feel validated.   
  
I do this as a hobby and enjoy it as such! I used to work in games industry, so for me it's like returning to a discipline I hadn't thought much about for a decade, and seeing that I can do things that previously in the studio I worked for took whole teams. 

People say "AGI" is some vague term and I am confused bc I always thought it meant something around "generally able to replace most economically valuable human labour" and while we are mercifully not at that point yet, if you are old like me, worked in game studio like me, you can see there is a pretty dramatic change already well underway. 

I personally love it, and feel very encouraged by it. I think game-making is an ancient and deeply human form of storytelling. The more hoomans that are able to tell their stories and make their ideas into shareable tangible realities, the better off I think human culture is. 

So my "expectation" if we're gonna throw that around is more cultural-level not individual, and about what it can do for us as a global village when storytelling gets easier and easier. Sharing, already, was what the internet gave us. Creating is what comes next perhaps. I like to be optimistic about this aspect.

comments.author: Schnitzhole
comments.body:
I do it for the love of the game but I would be fine making net $0 if it covers the cost of listing the game and all that.

Even steam charges $100 to list your free game and app stores even more.

comments.author: mahrogamers
comments.body: I think it all comes down to having something inside you that you genuinely want to create first. Once you achieve that, you naturally hope it can make you some money too
